text:
Lina: Quick recap from the spike — proposing we carve out the "ghost-adapter" as a thin facade that forwards hotpath requests to the runtime plane. Goals: isolate model-specific enrichment, reduce churn in runtime, and let infra autoscale independently.

Samir: Ran the load spike this morning. Observed ~12% reduction in P95 under steady traffic. Cold-path RPCs added ~10–20ms due to an extra hop. No correctness regressions.
Bench: http://bench.internal/ghost-spike (internal)

Ezra: Pushed a tiny manifest for how the adapter would run in a pool. Example run config:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ghost-adapter
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ghost-adapter
        image: redwood/ghost-adapter:canary
        env:
        - name: LOG_LEVEL
          value: info
```

Rachel: Ops concerns:
- Session ownership swap needs a migration plan (session.meta.owner)
- Cache-warming: recommend a prefix-warm job during canary
- Rollback fast path requires a traffic-surge guard

Lina: Rollout proposal: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 days, with automated rollback if P99 increases by >5%. Feature flag: `ghost_adapter` in platform config. Tracing: attach `x-ghost-trace` header for first 72h.

Samir: Ownership suggestion: eng-runtime retains RPC contract, eng-platform owns flagging and rollout, eng-infra owns HPA tuning. We should create a short-lived "adapter" subteam to shepherd cutover.

deploy-bot: Canary job queued: `canary/ghost-adapter/2024-07-15-09:12` — staging->canary scheduled.

Lina: Decision: approve pilot. Action items:
- Lina: write runbook + rollback steps (due EOD Fri)
- Samir: PR with config and metrics dashboard (open by Tue)
- Rachel: schedule warm-job and oncall rotation (by next Wed)

Samir: :rocket:
Rachel: :thumbsup:
Ezra: Good catch on the cache job, will prototype
